/LILIAN

Baltic Exchange Market Report 09 October 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 2917 (-56)
Baltic Capesize Index: 4340 (-172)
Baltic Panamax Index: 2424 (14)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1814 (6)
Baltic Handysize Index: 996 (-4)
CAPESIZE
The market ended the week on a softer note, with the BCI 182 5TC dropping by $1,560 to close at $39,363. In the Pacific, the C5 index slipped by $0.490 to $14.235, while the Atlantic continued to lose ground, with C3 falling by $0.431 to $33.294.Despite another busy week of fixing activity on C5, the market struggled to build on the gains seen earlier in the week. With last-done levels in the upper $14s, owners started the day with bullish expectations, with offers said to be approaching $16.00. However, this optimism proved short-lived, and as the day progressed, reports emerged of one miner paying $14.20 on a couple of occasions, while another was heard to have fixed at $14.15. With only two C5 miners active today, the market finished below recent levels despite the considerable volume of business concluded throughout the week. The Atlantic remained subdued into the close, with sentiment continuing to soften amid limited activity. On C3, reports of $33.00 being paid for split dates set the tone as the week drew to a close. Overall, the week ended with both basins under pressure, as a busy Pacific fixing programme failed to translate into sustained upward momentum, while the Atlantic continued to struggle for support.
PANAMAX
Today marked a quieter end to the week, although sentiment remained positive, with the P5TC rising by $125 to finish at $21,813. Market sources reported slower activity in the Atlantic, with both trans-Atlantic and fronthaul routes seeing fewer fresh fixtures as charterers and owners appeared content to pause following the week's busier trading. Despite the slowdown, owners are said to remain optimistic about the market's near-term prospects, supported by the increase in activity and improving rate levels seen over recent days. In the Pacific, market sources continued to describe fundamentals as broadly balanced, leaving little room for movement between bids and offers. Demand from Australia and the North Pacific is said to remain steady, helping to underpin sentiment, although a lack of fresh catalysts has kept rate fluctuations to a minimum.
SUPRAMAX
A slow end to a rather dull week. Despite the holidays in Asia the market creep up in the East, and was the main driver for the Index which finished the week up $78 to close at $22,929, up $310 from last Friday. Whilst NoPac saw the biggest gains, steady backhaul enquiries and a steady demand from south east Asia all helped the market, although some suggested a growing tonnage list has yet to have an impact. The Atlantic has been very positional with the US Gulf softening especially for fronthauls, and the south also showing a softer tone, although against some resistance from Owners. The Continent was said to be quieter today, but levels are still strong, and the Mediterranean has seen a much needed increase in demand now.
HANDYSIZE
It was a typically quiet end-of-week session, with minimal activity and limited fresh information emerging. The BHSI fell by 4 points to 996, while the 7TC average declined by $78 to close at $17,926. Activity in the Continent and Mediterranean was quieter, with few fixtures reported and rates remaining broadly flat. The HSL Geraldton (40,528 2025) open Dunkirk on 15–16 October was fixed for a trip via COGH to the Far East in the high $20,000s, although further details were not disclosed. The South Atlantic remained firm, with fresh demand supporting higher rates. By contrast, the US Gulf continued to face pressure, as demand remained insufficient to absorb the growing tonnage list. In Asia, activity was also muted, with few fresh updates. The Devbulk Demet (31,018 2012) was fixed from Salaverry with redelivery in the China–Japan range at $14,500 for the first 62 days and $15,500 thereafter, or at the charterers’ option, $16,000 for two to three laden legs, although further details were not disclosed. Period activity also emerged, with a 41,000-dwt vessel open in South China on 7–10 October reported fixed for 4 to 6 months at $20,250, again with further details lacking.
